newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares soar on expectation of new govt.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares soar on expectation of new govt.

text.p: Istanbul shares soared on Thursday amid strong liquidity influx boosted by growing market expectations that a new secularist alliance may replace the ruling Islamist-led coalition government, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,515, up 78 points or 5.43 percent from Wednesday. Trade volume surged to 24.47 trillion lira ($178.7 million) from Wednesday's 16.31 trillion ($118.7 million).

Three-day gains triggered by the rising prospect of a new government reached 8.6 percent, after a 8.9 percent slump on political fears to Monday's 1,395 close from April 24 opening which followed a 6-1/2 day holiday.
"The expectation that the ruling coalition will fall moved the market which was tired of the recent political uncertainty that lasted for weeks," said Tunc Tuncer from Aks securities.

"But I think this positive effect will be short lived. There will be problems in the decision making processes of a (new) multi-party coalition in the medium term and these will have negative impacts on the market," he added.
Turkish conservative leader Mesut Yilmaz said on Thursday opposition MPs were aiming to submit a censure motion by the weekend to topple the Islamist - conservative coalition.
Opposition and dissident government MPs have been negotiating the fall of the government for some time.

"Purchases by foreign investors created an important cash entry in the last few days. There is also cash coming from domestic institutional investors. The fading of political uncertainty since yesterday helped to spark a sharp rise," said Tayfun Oral from Ata securities.
"Sharply higher volume is a healthy sign. If there is no political crisis and early elections do not come on the agenda, the rise may continue," he added.
Some brokers await profit-taking on Friday as players may not want to take risks ahead of the weekend.
